Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.mfa

Class TrustedDeviceFilter

java.lang.Object
org.springframework.web.filter.GenericFilterBean
org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.mfa.TrustedDeviceFilter
All Implemented Interfaces:
jakarta.servlet.Filter, org.springframework.beans.factory.Aware, org.springframework.beans.factory.BeanNameAware, org.springframework.beans.factory.DisposableBean, org.springframework.beans.factory.InitializingBean, org.springframework.context.EnvironmentAware, org.springframework.core.env.EnvironmentCapable, org.springframework.web.context.ServletContextAware
public class TrustedDeviceFilter extends org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter
Lets a browser that was trusted earlier skip the second factor of a sign-in. The cookie is only looked at where it matters: on the second-factor page (GET /login/second-factor), where every request that owes a second factor is sent. Every other request goes through untouched, so a user who never gets the factor is not looked up on each request. When a signed-in user that does not hold the TrustedDeviceFactor yet reaches that page with the __Host-TRUSTED-DEVICE cookie, and its signed value belongs to a device of that same user that has neither expired nor been revoked, the authentication of the session is replaced by one that also holds the factor authority (a remembered factor: it satisfies the sign-in policy but is never reported in the tokens), the session id is changed, the session is saved and the request that was interrupted is resumed instead of asking for a code. A forged or unsigned value is rejected by FindTrustedDeviceUseCase before anything is looked up. While a step-up is pending (SecondFactorRequiredEntryPoint.isStepUpPending(jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest)) the cookie is ignored: a trusted device cannot satisfy it, so the page is rendered and asks for a real second factor.
